note: Every external dataset held under raw/. The FILES are gitignored (3.4 GB, and all re-downloadable from the documented sources); THIS RECORD is committed, so the repository always knows what was collected, under what licence, and why it was kept - even on a machine where the files are absent.
rule: A dataset that is not in the cube is not thereby useless. Three intakes: cube (mineral quantity per country-year), driver (activity series per country-year), reference (everything a question might need later). A non-CC licence permits use but never redistribution in out/.

library.dataset: CEPII BACI bilateral trade, HS02 and HS17 vintages
library.licence: Etalab Open Licence 2.0 (redistribution permitted, attribution required)
library.why_we_might_need_it: HS02 gives 2002-2024 on one nomenclature. Only the 47 mapped codes are ingested; the rest is deliberate ballast left out. LICENCE CORRECTED 6 Sep 2026: this was recorded as "Free for research", which understated it and would have blocked republication. CEPII licenses BACI under Etalab 2.0 - an open licence permitting reproduction, redistribution and commercial reuse with attribution, and declared compatible with CC BY 4.0 - so the BACI-derived rows in out/cube.csv.gz are properly published, not a leak. Required citation: Gaulier, G. and Zignago, S. (2010), BACI: International Trade Database at the Product-Level.

library.dataset: BGS World Mineral Statistics full panel
library.why_we_might_need_it: The spine: 410k records, production + trade by country, 1970-2024.
Workforce and participation indicators for the energy sector. No material dimension; kept for completeness of the collection.

library.dataset: OECD International Transport and Insurance Costs of merchandise trade (ITIC)
library.licence: OECD Terms and Conditions - redistribution and commercial use permitted with attribution; acknowledgment must propagate to sub-licensees
library.why_we_might_need_it: The published CIF/FOB margin per importer-exporter-HS2017 heading-year, 976,568 observations 2015-2024. It REPLACED our own freight estimation entirely: the per-product medians, the borrowed CEPII 2008 coefficients, the locally-anchored level and our invented 10% ceiling are all now fallback that fires zero times. Verbatim from the terms, checked 6 Sep 2026: "you can extract from, download, copy, adapt, print, distribute, share and embed Data for any purpose, even for commercial use. You must give appropriate credit to the OECD by using the citation associated with the relevant Data." Caveat in the same terms: some content may be owned by third parties and the user is responsible for checking - ITIC is an OECD statistical product built from member reporting, so this is noted rather than resolved. Cite as: OECD (2026), International Transport and Insurance Costs of merchandise trade (ITIC), OECD Data Explorer, accessed 6 September 2026. NOTE 95% of margins are gravity-model imputations (OBS_STATUS I), not reported values - published is not the same as observed.
Where a cited figure can be re-checked against the document it came from.

The one I wrongly dismissed. Drought curtails hydro, and hydro curtailment curtails ALUMINIUM and silicon smelting - Yunnan is the documented case. A weather series is a real explanatory variable for why refined output moves in a year when capacity did not.

library.dataset: IEA activity datasets: Energy & AI annex, Value Added DB, EEI Highlights
library.licence: MIXED - Energy&AI is CC BY 4.0; Value Added and EEI are NOT CC
library.why_we_might_need_it: Country-year ACTIVITY series for the consumption model (demand = activity x intensity). Value added by ISIC division is the driver the IEA itself uses. The non-CC two may be used but never redistributed in out/.
RESERVES, refinery output, import reliance and recycling are still unextracted - the largest known unopened box in the library.
Mirror side of the trade reconciliation.
Deposit records, site grain.

library.licence: NOT CC - Terms of Use for Non-CC Material
library.why_we_might_need_it: Refreshes the existing `elec` driver, and monthly grain makes it the natural series for testing whether smelting output tracks power availability.

library.dataset: IEA Critical Minerals Dataset + report PDFs
library.why_we_might_need_it: Base-year supply by country at mine AND refining stage - the layer where BGS is thinnest. Two editions held, two missing.
Distance/contiguity for trade-gravity and reallocation work.

library.licence: NOT CC - Terms of Use for Non-CC Material
library.why_we_might_need_it: Energy balances for 185+ countries. Industrial energy use is a broad activity proxy where no physical output series exists, and the balance structure names the industry sectors.

library.dataset: IEA Energy Technology RD&D Budgets (public + private), 1974-2025
library.licence: NOT CC - Terms of Use for Non-CC Material
library.why_we_might_need_it: Country-year-technology R&D SPEND. Money, not an activity a material intensity can multiply, so not a driver. Kept because it is the best public measure of how hard a country is trying on a technology - a possible leading indicator for deployment, and a possible read on SUBSTITUTION effort, which the atlas already has a layer for. Not redistributable.

library.licence: NOT CC - Terms of Use for Non-CC Material
library.why_we_might_need_it: Energy spend by household. Affordability context, no material link.
Criticality scores and end-use shares - indicators ABOUT materials, so a dimension rather than cube rows. Also the list vintages used for the ex-ante freeze test.
Depth to 1900 and world production totals. Found by the catalog after sitting unused except for its price column.

Country-specific reserves and production where a survey publishes better than the global compilations.

library.licence: NOT CC - Terms of Use for Non-CC Material
library.why_we_might_need_it: The source behind our existing `ev` driver. EV sales and stock by country-year, and the battery chemistry splits that decide whether a marginal EV pulls lithium/cobalt/nickel or LFP.

library.licence: NOT CC - Terms of Use for Non-CC Material
library.why_we_might_need_it: Emissions by country-year. Relevant if an embodied-emissions layer is ever built on top of the material flows.

library.dataset: Activity drivers: steel, vehicles, EV, electricity, solar, wind, cement, population, aerospace, semiconductors...
library.why_we_might_need_it: The inputs to the consumption model. Any new driver lands here.

library.licence: NOT CC - Terms of Use for Non-CC Material
library.why_we_might_need_it: End-use energy prices. The nearest public proxy for the energy cost faced by industry, which is what actually decides smelter economics.

library.dataset: Oil and gas field decline rates
library.why_we_might_need_it: Decline-rate methodology. Directly analogous to ore-grade decline in mining, which is a question the atlas has not yet asked and probably should.
Infrastructure geometry (ports, rail) for logistics work.

library.dataset: Hydrogen Production and Infrastructure Projects Database
library.why_we_might_need_it: Project grain, so not cube material - but electrolysers consume iridium and platinum, so this is the demand side of a PGM story the atlas already tells from the supply side.
Investment by sector and region.
Investment by sector and region.

Latest edition. Six editions together give an investment TIME SERIES by sector - a leading indicator for the capacity that later consumes metal, and one of the few places where the older editions are worth keeping rather than superseded.

library.licence: RESTRICTED - fee required for use in modelling / derived products
library.why_we_might_need_it: LICENCE-BLOCKED, not merely non-CC: the terms require a paid Licence Agreement to use this data "in any type of modelling for the purpose of creating derived data or derived products" - which is exactly what every page here is. Held for reference so the decision is inspectable and nobody re-downloads it to ask again. Also a 2018-vintage scenario set, superseded several times.

library.why_we_might_need_it: Access rates by country-year. The material link is indirect but real: closing an access gap means grid, which means conductor - it needs a published km-per-connection intensity to become anything more than a narrative.

library.licence: NOT CC - Terms of Use for Non-CC Material

Investment by sector and region.

library.dataset: World Mining Data 6.4, production by country
library.why_we_might_need_it: The only source that marks every cell reported vs estimated.
Facility-level buildup behind selected chains.

Consumption subsidies by country-year. Not a material series - but energy price support is one of the real reasons SMELTING locates where it does (aluminium and silicon are power-cost industries). If the chokepoint map is ever pushed from "where refining is" to "why it is there", this is an input to that argument.
DIRECTLY relevant to the cobalt gap: BGS under-reports DRC precisely because artisanal output does not enter national returns.
The midstream layer behind the chokepoint map.
Refining concentration where USGS measures it directly.
Entity reconciliation helper.
